latest_nl_proof:
Let
D := Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_i - Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_{m+1-i}.

For the second sum, reindex by j = m+1-i. Then
Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_{m+1-i} = Σ_{j=1}^m x_{m+1-j} w_j,
so
D = Σ_{i=1}^m (x_i - x_{m+1-i}) w_i.

Now pair the terms with indices i and m+1-i. For each i = 1, ..., ⌊m/2⌋, the contribution of this pair is
(x_i - x_{m+1-i}) w_i + (x_{m+1-i} - x_i) w_{m+1-i}
= (x_i - x_{m+1-i})(w_i - w_{m+1-i}).
If m is odd, the middle term i = (m+1)/2 is 0 because x_i - x_{m+1-i} = 0 there. Hence
D = Σ_{i=1}^{⌊m/2⌋} (x_i - x_{m+1-i})(w_i - w_{m+1-i}).

Assume first that x_1 ≥ x_2 ≥ ... ≥ x_m. Then for every i ≤ ⌊m/2⌋ we have i < m+1-i, so
x_i ≥ x_{m+1-i}
and, because w_1 > w_2 > ... > w_m,
w_i > w_{m+1-i}.
Therefore every summand in the last expression for D is nonnegative, so D ≥ 0. This is exactly
Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_i ≥ Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_{m+1-i}.

If in addition x is nonconstant, then a nonincreasing nonconstant vector must satisfy x_1 > x_m. Since also w_1 > w_m, the i=1 summand
(x_1 - x_m)(w_1 - w_m)
is strictly positive. All other summands are nonnegative, so D > 0. Thus the inequality is strict when x is nonconstant.

Now assume instead that x_1 ≤ x_2 ≤ ... ≤ x_m. Define
E := Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_{m+1-i} - Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_i.
Reindex the first sum exactly as above:
Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_{m+1-i} = Σ_{i=1}^m x_{m+1-i} w_i.
Hence
E = Σ_{i=1}^m (x_{m+1-i} - x_i) w_i.
Pairing i with m+1-i gives
E = Σ_{i=1}^{⌊m/2⌋} (x_{m+1-i} - x_i)(w_i - w_{m+1-i}).
For each i ≤ ⌊m/2⌋ we have x_{m+1-i} ≥ x_i because x is nondecreasing, and still w_i > w_{m+1-i} because w is strictly decreasing. So each summand is nonnegative, and therefore E ≥ 0. This is exactly
Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_{m+1-i} ≥ Σ_{i=1}^m x_i w_i.

If x is nonconstant, then a nondecreasing nonconstant vector satisfies x_m > x_1. Since w_1 > w_m, the i=1 summand
(x_m - x_1)(w_1 - w_m)
is strictly positive, so E > 0. Thus the inequality is strict when x is nonconstant.

This proves both assertions.
role_in_parent: This is a support lemma for comparing the two alternating continuations; it is used inside the proof chain leading to L6.
statement_nl: Let m be a positive integer. Let x=(x_1,...,x_m) be a nonnegative vector and let w=(w_1,...,w_m) be a positive vector with w_1 > w_2 > ... > w_m. If x_1 >= x_2 >= ... >= x_m, then sum_{i=1}^m x_i w_i >= sum_{i=1}^m x_i w_{m+1-i}, and the inequality is strict when x is nonconstant. If x_1 <= x_2 <= ... <= x_m, then sum_{i=1}^m x_i w_{m+1-i} >= sum_{i=1}^m x_i w_i, and the inequality is strict when x is nonconstant.

domain_restrictions: each entry of x is nonnegative
each entry of w is positive
w_1 is greater than w_2, which is greater than w_3, and so on down to w_m
the comparisons among the x_i are entrywise comparisons of real numbers
nonconstant means not all entries of x are equal
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integer m, every nonnegative real vector x of length m, and every positive real vector w of length m that is strictly decreasing, the following hold. If x is nonincreasing, then the dot product of x with w is at least the dot product of x with the reversed vector w, and this is strict when x is not constant. If x is nondecreasing, then the dot product of x with the reversed vector w is at least the dot product of x with w, and this is strict when x is not constant.
quantifier_order: for every real vector x of length m with nonnegative entries
for every real vector w of length m with positive entries and strict decrease from first to last entry
if x is nonincreasing, then the sum with matching order is at least the sum with reversed weights, and the inequality is strict when x is not constant
if x is nondecreasing, then the sum with reversed weights is at least the sum with matching order, and the inequality is strict when x is not constant

variables.domain: real vectors of length m with all entries nonnegative
variables.name: x
variables.role: input vector whose monotonicity controls the comparison

variables.domain: real vectors of length m with all entries positive and strictly decreasing
variables.name: w

variables.domain: the i-th component of x for each index i from 1 to m
variables.name: x_i

variables.domain: the i-th component of w for each index i from 1 to m
variables.name: w_i

witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses in the statement
The strictness clause depends on the same x and w as the weak inequality, with the extra condition that x is not constant
